text.p: IBM Corp and 3Com Corp said Wednesday they plan a significant expansion of their existing networking alliance in the areas of office workgroup and building-to-building campus backbone networks.
The companies said they had agreed to further technology exchanges and a remarketing pact as part of the expanded pact.

They said the new systems will allow customers to more quickly install and use high-data-bandwidth applications like videoconferencing, online financial trading, distance learning, medical imaging, and electronic banking and shopping.
IBM and 3Com said they plan to exchange technologies for future high-end campus backbone switches.

They plan to make use of IBM's next-generation Prizma Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) chip sets and 3Com's Ethernet-to-ATM ZipChip switching technologies. ATM is a high-speed technology designed to handle voice, video and data traffic over a network. Ethernet is the most popular existing network technology, which 3Com has beefed up to work with ATM.
In addition, 3Com plans to remarket IBM's Multiprotocol Switched Services to add enriched ATM features to 3Com's existing ATM Local Area Network Emulation (LANE) services.

The result will be products capable of handling network traffic based on a variety of standards and to give Token Ring, the standard network technology used in mainframe computer-based networks, LANE functions.
IBM said it plans to offer its own versions of 3Com's SuperStack II 1000 and 3000 workgroup switches aimed at corporate department level workgroups.
It also said it plans to provide ATM connections for certain models of future IBM and 3Com workgroup switches.

IBM said it plans to integrate 3Com's Fast Ethernet and future Gigabit Ethernet technology into the IBM 8260 and Super 8260 campus backbone switches, offering its customers a path to upgrade to the latest high-speed network technologies.
3Com stock was up nearly 2 points to 58-3/8 and was among the top five most active stocks on the Nasdaq. IBM was up 1-7/8 to 104-7/8, also in active trading, on the NYSE.
